beats.text: Effects sync with the outside world.
beats.say: use Effect lets a component synchronize with something outside of React: a server, a browser A P I, a timer. You write the setup, and optionally return a cleanup function that undoes it.

items: [a, b]  reruns when a or b change
List every value the effect uses
beats.say: The dependency array decides when the effect runs. An empty array means once, after the first render. A list reruns it when any value changes. No array means after every render. And you must list every value the effect reads.
Think of it as setup and cleanup pairs. On mount, setup runs. When a dependency changes, React runs the old cleanup first, then the new setup. And on unmount, the final cleanup runs.
When an effect fetches data, a slow earlier request can arrive after a newer one and overwrite it. A simple ignore flag, set in the cleanup, makes sure only the latest request updates state.

beats.text: Why effects run twice in development.

right.title: What it tests
items: Can the effect run twice safely?

beats.say: In development, Strict Mode mounts, unmounts, and mounts your component again. It's not a bug. It is a test that your cleanup is correct, and that the effect is safe to run twice.

Common pitfalls: missing dependencies give you stale values, objects created during render change every time, the effect callback can't be async itself, and effects are not for computing values you can derive.
